workarounds.symptom: uv lock --check reports multiple matches when a dependency has no package entry
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Report missing package entries for dependencies in `uv.lock`. Target files: crates/uv-lock/src/lock/mod.rs, crates/uv/tests/lock/lock.rs. workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Helm migration Job OOMKilled at 1Gi since v1.105.x — prisma_migration.py runs prisma generate after migrating (1.15 GiB peak for a step that can't succeed in the non_root image)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(proxy): skip prisma generate in the migration job when the prisma package is not writable. Target files: litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py, tests/unit/proxy/test_prisma_migration.py. The Helm migration Job was OOMKilled at a 1Gi limit after its migrations had already applied, because it still spawned `prisma generate`, which can never succeed on a read-only root. This skips that step when the installed prisma package is not writable and keeps using the client baked into the image. (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/52460)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]:
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(security): let the agent read the images GAIA generated. Target files: src/gaia/agents/tools/shell_tools.py, src/gaia/config.py, src/gaia/sd/mixin.py. After generating an image, asking GAIA to describe or use it failed with "Access denied … No approval can grant it", because images are saved inside the protected `~/.gaia` folder. Now the agent can read the images it generated there; everything else in `~/.gaia` (config, keys, tokens, memory, logs) stays blocked, and nothing can be written into the images folder. (Ref: https://github.com/amd/gaia/pull/8478)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: v0.25.1 streaming input beyond max_model_len produces negative scheduled token counts and crashes V2 runner
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Bugfix][Core] Drop streaming updates that would overflow max_model_len. Target files: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py, tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py, tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py. Streaming-input sessions merged the next input chunk into their prompt without checking the accumulated length against `max_model_len`, wedging or crashing the engine. This PR rejects such an update at merge time, parks the session so a shorter update can continue it, and adds scheduler-level and e2e regression tests. (Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63113)
